There are 13 subsidiary shrines within the precincts: Sakagami Shrine (Shikiuchi), Kamota Shrine (Shikinai), Daijinja, Sumiyoshi, Amaterasu, Hachiman, Kasuga, Kumano, Hakusan, Benten, Inari, Fukuishi, and Suitengu, which are collectively known as Arayama Shrine.

The style is Sangensha irimoya-zukuri, with a houndstooth gable in front, a large bower, and an eaves-shaped gable. The {{ill|kaerumata|ja|蟇股|qid=Q123117911}} in the upper center of the prayer pillar has dragons, clouds, and waves, and the left and right toad-mata have peonies and Chinese lions on the obverse, clouds and jewels on the back, and inside. The front center of the Honagoshi is carved with paulownia, the right one is carved with a horse mackerel, the left one is carved with sasanqua flowers, pine trees, and coins, and the north and south sides are carved with carp, pine, waterfalls, and clouds. The {{ill|tabasami|ja|手挟|qid=Q124660898}} of the facing prayer is {{ill|Sukashibori|fr|Sukashibori|ja|透彫|qid=Q17055244}}, and there are two on the left and right; the right side has a Basho and mantis carved on the right side, a lotus on the water on the left side, seaweed and shellfish on the right side, and irises on the left side. The wooden nose of Mukaihai has a strange and unusual shape resembling the head of an animal. This is said to be the only sculpture in the country of Basho with a mantis. According to the ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=surname record}}'' and the various clans of Izumi Province, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nao Ikebe}} is the same ancestor as {{ill|Sakanoue clan|de|Sakanoue|ja|坂上氏|uk|Саканоуе|zh|坂上氏|qid=Q10928477|lt=Sakagami Ōsukune}} and a descendant of King Achi. Furthermore, in the section of ``Izumi Province Jinmyocho'' {{ill|Ōtori district|ja|大鳥郡|zh|大鳥郡|qid=Q3270651}}, the three shrines of Ikebe Hinohara Shrine, Ikebe Shrine Shrine, and Ikebe Shrine, which are listed between Kusakabe Otoshi Shrine, Jindai Shrine, Sakanoue Shrine, and others, are thought to be shrines located in Hachita-go or Kusakabe-go, based on the order in which they are listed. Based on these facts, it is speculated that the Sakagami Shrine located in Hirai, Hachita-go was where the Ikebe clan or the Sakagami clan enshrined their ancestor {{ill|Achi no Omi|de|Achi no Omi|ja|阿知使主|zh|阿知使主|qid=Q11657596}} (Achi King). ``Sakai City History Sequel'' Volume 1 (Part 1, Ancient times, p. 179) states that there is a strong possibility that the Ikebe Nao family lived in Otori County in ancient times.

Although he left his hometown at a young age, he had a deep reverence for Tajihayahime Shrine and even visited it when he was a lieutenant colonel. A large plaque with the name of Navy Vice Admiral Kantaro Suzuki written on it, ``Respectful God, Worshipful Ancestor,'' still remains, and is currently hung in the parishioners gathering hall, and fans with the same inscription were reproduced and divided among the parishioners. When the main hall of the Inari Shrine, a shrine within the shrine precincts, was renovated and a new Tamagaki constructed in 1921, the Tamagaki stone dedicated in the name of Navy Vice Admiral Kantaro Suzuki remains. Also, when he was seriously injured in the {{ill|February 26 incident|ar|حادثة 26 فبراير|azb|۲۶ فوریه اوْلایی|cs|Incident 26. února|de|Putschversuch in Japan vom 26. Februar 1936|el|Στρατιωτικό κίνημα στην Ιαπωνία (1936)|es|Incidente del 26 de febrero|et|26. veebruari riigipöördekatse|fa|حادثه ۲۶ فوریه|fi|Helmikuun 26. päivän välikohtaus|fr|Incident du 26 Février|he|מרד הנפל של 26 בפברואר 1936|hu|Február 26-i incidens|id|Insiden 26 Februari|it|Incidente del 26 febbraio|ja|二・二六事件|ko|2·26 사건|krc|Джаш абычарланы путчу|nl|Mislukte staatsgreep in Japan van 26 februari 1936|pl|Incydent z 26 lutego|pt|Incidente de 26 de fevereiro|ru|Инцидент 26 февраля|sh|Incident 26. februara|simple|February 26 incident|sv|26 februari-incidenten|th|เหตุการณ์ 26 กุมภาพันธ์|tr|26 Şubat Olayı|uk|Інцидент 26 лютого|zh|二二六事件|zh_yue|二二六事件|qid=Q477958}}, Tajisahime no Mikoto stood at his bedside and saved his life, and in January of the following year, he and his wife Taka visited the shrine to commemorate his return. After the war, when the idea of ​​building Suzuki Shrine came up, it was discussed that the grounds of Tajiwa Hime Shrine would be suitable.
